newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Macintosh aims for better spread of sites.
newsitem.headline: Macintosh aims for better spread of sites.

text.p: Dutch retailer Macintosh NV said on Thursday it was seeking a better spread of its floorspace between out-of-town and downtown locations.
"I think out-of-town and downtown formulas are highly compatible. We want to have both," chairman Gert Beijer said.
Beijer said the opening of big out-of-town shopping centres also stimulated shopping activity in town centres.

At present most of Macintosh's stores are in out-of-town locations, but last week the company said it was in talks to buy a 50-percent stake in shoe retailer Hoogenbosch, whose stores are mainly located at prime sites in town centres.

"We now are at the stage of the due diligence and we would not have taken this first step unless we were fairly sure of taking the second step (exercising an option to buy the remaining 50 percent) too," Beijer told reporters.
Beijers said he also saw good prospects for out-of-town shopping centers due in part to recent changes in regulations.
The retail group earlier reported 1996 net profit fell to 2.7 million guilders from 22.5 million in 1995.
